messages.author: bb61319f77c96595
messages.subject: plot_coef
parts:
Dear Karl,

I would like to ask about function ‘plot_coef’ in R/qtl2.
I have analysed HS rats data. These rats were from 8 founder strains, namely:”ACI, BN, BUF, F344, M520, MR, WN and WKY”. 
My cross2 data file named ‘do.hap’. I noticed that only do.hap$founder_geno has information these 8 founder strains, with the order is the same as I listed above.

The output plot from  ‘plot_coef’ shows “A,B,C,…,H” for 8 founder strains, instead of using real names of strains. (while the plot_coefCC gives names for CC rats - which are different)

My questions are:
1. How can I have correct names for 8 founder strains in the output plot?
2. If I have to add this information manually, I need to be sure that the order I typed in is correct with the order in the result (output from 'scan1blup'). Is the order in the result the same with the order in the  do.hap$founder_geno? I find a bit hard to explain this question, hope you understand what I mean...

Thank you for your help!

Best wishes,
Thu

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: plot_coef
parts:
The column names in do.hap$founder_geno don't get used.

You can control the allele labels in a couple of ways. You can provide them with the argument legend_lab, like so:

strains <- c("ACI", "BN", "BUF", "F344", "M520", "MR", "WN",  "WKY")
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", legend_lab=strains)

Or if you provide colors with col, if that vector has names, they are used.

my_colors <- CCcolors
names(my_colors) <- strains
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", col=my_colors)

The colum names in the output of scan1coef() are taken from the names in the genotype or allele probabilities that are provided, and those are taken from do.hap$alleles, which are generally single letters so that the labels for genotypes become two-letter strings rather than something unwieldy like "ACIACI" or "ACIBN".

The order of the founder strains in the allele probabilities is as in do.hap$founder_geno, so you could take the names from there:

my_colors <- CCcolors
names(my_colors) <- rownames( do.hap$founder_geno[[1]] )
plot_coef(co, pmap, legend="topleft", col=my_colors)

karl

messages.author: bb61319f77c96595
messages.subject: Re: plot_coef
parts:
Hi Karl again,

I still have a question about plot_coef to ask you. How can we plot only region on a chromosome using this function?

What I am doing so far are:
1. Estimate QTL effect for chromosome (chr) having QTL with scan1coef
coef <- scan1coef(apr[,chr], do.pheno.final[,2, drop=FALSE], kinship_loco[[chr]], addcovar, cores=4)
2. Subset pmap for the region of interest (left,right)
       pmap_chr <- unlist(do.hap$pmap[chr])
       pmap_sub <- list(pmap_chr[pmap_chr > left & pmap_chr < right])
       names(pmap_sub) <- c(chr)
3. Plot using plot_coef for that region
plot_coef(x = coef, map = pmap_sub, scan1_output=qtl2.scan, columns=1:8, bgcolor="gray95", legend="bottomright", col=my_colors, main = paste("coef.QTL effect.Chr",chr,".",left,".",right,".",trait))

This does not work with error about no common makers between pmap_sub and scan1_output. This seems caused by the format of pmap_sub.
If I do this way, it works:
       pmap_chr <- do.hap$pmap$"6"         # assume chr=6
       pmap_sub <- list(pmap_chr[pmap_chr > left & pmap_chr < right])
       names(pmap_sub) <- c(chr)
However, it is not so convenient where I have to specify which chromosome instead of using a variable 'chr'.

I might miss some of your functions.. Please tell me if you know the best way to do it. Many thanks!

Best wishes,
Thu
